question.text: According to the worked example on pp.320-321 of the NISM-Series-XXI-B workbook, in an alpha-beta separation construction the portfolio manager combines which of the following positions to isolate alpha from market beta (as the workbook literally states)?

answer.text: Long active portfolio + Short market-neutral portfolio
Long active portfolio + Short broad-market index/futures
Long passive ETF + Short active portfolio
Long active portfolio + Long broad-market index

explanation.text: The Logic: The NISM-Series-XXI-B workbook example on p.321 describes the alpha-beta separation construction literally as taking a long position on the active portfolio and a short position on the market-neutral portfolio. The stem is anchored to that source text, so the keyed answer is the option that matches the workbook wording exactly. The Trap: "Long active + short broad-market index/futures" is the finance-logic answer one would expect, since a market-neutral portfolio has zero beta and therefore cannot strip market beta from the active book — but the workbook example uses the market-neutral wording, and exam answers must follow the workbook. "Long passive ETF + short active portfolio" reverses the alpha sign. "Long active + long broad-market index" doubles beta exposure rather than removing it. In the audit-flagged original, both the workbook-literal and the finance-logic answers could be defended. Note: The original stem was ambiguous because the keyed answer matched finance logic (short broad-market index/futures) while the cited workbook example (p.321) literally pairs the long active portfolio with a short market-neutral portfolio. The stem has been tightened to ask for the workbook's literal construction, and the key has been flipped to the option that quotes the workbook directly, making the answer unambiguous.
